title: Set a specimen pan across a toilet bowl under the raised seat, both wings on the rim, and lower the seat onto them
instruction: Lift the toilet seat, set the specimen pan upright across the bowl opening with both wings on the rim, lower the seat onto the wings, then let go and move both hands clear.
context: The hard parts: the seat is lifted and kept up while the pan goes under it (its check hinges hold it only past upright, which here it cannot reach: it would lean into the robot's left arm, so a hand holds it); the pan is turned 90 degrees and set across the opening: set down lengthwise it drops through (222.3 x 336.6 mm into a 248 x 373 mm opening), across it bridges with 44 mm of wing on the rim each side; then the seat is lowered onto the wings, not dropped, and both hands let go. A specimen pan under the toilet seat is how a nursing assistant collects urine or stool from a patient who can use the toilet. O*NET 31-1131.00 Nursing Assistants (1,505,900 employed, 2025) lists "Collect specimens, such as urine, feces, or sputum." (https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/31-1131.00). The seat is a Bemis 1955CT commercial open-front seat, the opening a Kohler K-4302 elongated bowl's, the pan a Medline 30 oz specimen collector pan.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left. A mock bowl rim: a 12 mm birch plywood frame on four 32 x 32 mm pine blocks 10.3 cm tall, its top 11.5 cm over the bench, screwed to the bench. Its opening is a Kohler K-4302 elongated bowl's, 24.8 cm across (x 15.6 to 40.4) and 37.3 cm long (y +19.0 to -18.3), cut as a rectangle; the frame is 36.8 cm across from y +2.5 to its front edge at y -22.0 and 31.0 cm across behind that, to its back edge at y +31.5. A Bemis 1955CT seat (white, open front, no cover, non self-sustaining check hinges) is bolted through two holes 5-1/2 in. apart on the frame's back (x 21.0 and 35.0, y +27.0), its front towards -y, closed on its bumpers; its check hinges stop it 11 degrees past upright, where it stays up. An empty Medline Specimen Collector Pan, 30 oz (DYND36600H) stands upright on the bench, its middle at (27.0, -43.0), lengthwise: its wings along y, within 3 mm of two pencil marks at its front wall's corners.
scoring: 0.0 for good if at any step the pan falls through the opening (its lowest point within 8 mm of the bench, its middle under the opening) or the seat is let go above 20 degrees (with no hand within 25 mm of it and not resting on the pan, it falls 2 deg or more from a height over 20 deg). Otherwise, at the end of the trial: 1.0: the pan across the opening: upright (tilt <= 8 deg), its wings within 20 deg of square across the opening, its middle inside the opening, both wing tips over the side rims with their undersides at most 5 mm over the rim top; the seat lowered onto the wings (at most 3 deg up, the ring over the middle of both wings); every part of both hands at least 30 mm from the seat, the pan and the deck; all held so for 1.0 s (20 steps) with the pan moving at most 1.5 mm and the seat at most 0.5 deg. 0.5: the pan across the opening as above, any 1.0 condition not met. 0.0: otherwise. On the bench: the fall through and the seat let go from the trial video (the time of each); tilt with a phone inclinometer on the pan's rim and on the seat; the wings on the rim and under the ring by eye and with a ruler; the hands and the 1.0 s from the video.
reset_notes: Between trials, about 1 minute: raise the seat, lift the pan off the rim (or from the bench under the opening if it fell through: then a clean pan), lower the seat onto its bumpers, and stand the pan lengthwise on its two pencil marks.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX, 240 Hz. Seat: one rigid ring of boxes (its oval outline drawn as boxes) with the maker's sizes and 1.91 kg on a free hinge to its check-hinge stop at 101 deg. Pan: a rigid shell of 4 mm boxes with the listed outside sizes; its thin walls and wings do not flex. Deck: fixed boxes, the bowl's oval opening cut as a 248 x 373 mm rectangle. Grippy friction (1.2/1.0) on seat and pan. No liquid. Nothing is welded, pushed, latched or placed.
